hook: SCP-1247 has one of the most absurd premises you will find: a man who perceives every animal as one particular Hollywood actor. Do not expect a pure joke, though. The history section turns grim, with years of isolation, hunting, eating what looks like human bodies, and a homicide and cannibalism investigation.
whyItMatters:
It is a strong example of a comedic hook used to deliver something sad. The precise, clinical testing language, applied to an actor galloping like a horse or lying paralyzed as a worm, keeps the humor dry and lets the later tragedy land harder.

It also shows how the containment section can quietly tell a story before the description does, through rules that only make sense once you understand what the subject lives with.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures read differently after the history. Masks for staff, no leather, no meat, no mirrors, the warning that he cannot tell organisms apart, and the precise height and weight required of anyone who touches him all reflect a world where every creature, and every piece of meat, looks like the same man. The one exception, an animal inside his own body appearing as it really is, explains why his cabin meals could only be identified by biting into them.

The cause is hinted at but never solved. A fungus resembling morels has replaced much of his brain, and his third effect is that he cannot see morels at all, so the thing changing him is the one thing he is unable to look at. The arrest that brought him in followed a killing with cannibalism thought to be tied to his animal hunts, and the article closes with the film he was watching found harmless and his lack of interest in seeing it again.
